script: Professional photographer knew better than three ophthalmologists. It cost him €750.. I was a qualified dispensing optician in France. My training was all about physiological optics and visual analysis. We tweak prescriptions when we have to, but we're not supposed to cook one up from scratch. (I am not saying it's a hard line—just saying it's the rule.) When I was still learning the ropes, a colleague of mine had a perfect malicious compliance moment with a customer. That dude walked in like he owned the place. He'd just seen three different ophthalmologists, gotten three different prescriptions, and decided to cherry‑pick the bits he liked. He was basically the king of "mix and match." (And that was the start of the chaos.) The worst part was his progressive lens addition. For those of you who don't know, the addition is the extra magnifying power at the bottom of the lens for reading. Usually it's the same for both eyes, unless you're dealing with a rare medical condition. This guy wanted one eye at 67 cm, the other at 40 cm. Like walking in a stiletto on one foot and a flat on the other—
